newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Airports Authority to raise $500 million.
newsitem.headline: Israel Airports Authority to raise $500 million.

text.p: Israel's Airports Authority will be seeking to raise as much as $500 million over the next five years to fund a major expansion of the country's main airport, an official at the authority said on Thursday.

The authority is moving ahead with plans after the national planning and development committee earlier this week approved the expansion project, which is called Ben-Gurion 2000, said Ya'acov Dayan, the authority's deputy managing director for finance.
"There are still approvals we need from the government and a detailed site plan that will take another month or two, if not more. In the meantime, we are preparing," Dayan told Reuters.
He said the Treasury had already approved plans to borrow $100 million from domestic banks and that afterwards the authority would make its first-ever overseas bond issue.
Dayan said the authority aims to raise $100 million to $150 million in the first issue.
All told, he estimated, the authority would be raising between $450 million and $500 million over the next five years, including the $100 million already approved.
"As the project progresses, we will raise money here and overseas. We will check which is the best alternative at each stage," Dayan said.
He estimated the budget for the Ben-Gurion 2000 project would be about $600 million. In addition, the authority has a regular development budget of $40 million to $50 million annually.
Dayan said the authority had already held preliminary discussions with several investment banks, including Lehman Brothers, Bear Sterns, Merrill Lynch and Bank of America.
